how-we-know: Build a worked comparison of one excavation record and one attributed account; explain why the unread Ogundiran lead cannot settle a page-specific claim.
land-and-language: Replace the broad regional sweep in a parallel layer with dated routes and two named localities; commission dialect-aware geographical review.
oduduwa: Place separately attributed town versions side by side; retain the difference between sacred beginning and independently dated settlement.
ile-ife: Use object accession records, find context and collection provenance as distinct narrative strands; pilot story now provides an optional model.
oyo: Develop one mapped, dated corridor case and test claims about imperial institutions against inspected archaeology and regional testimony.
regional-states: Give Ijebu, Owo, Ekiti and Ijesa separate case studies rather than treating their institutions as variations inferred from Oyo.
trade-economy: Follow a documented commodity and market institution through a specified place and period; keep coercion and enslavement visible where evidenced.
wars: Obtain full chronology sources and compare named community memories of one conflict; distinguish wartime testimony from later reconciliation narrative.
ibadan-abeokuta: Develop two separately sourced city histories and identify where comparison is analytical rather than a shared founding narrative.
faith: Anchor religious categories to named public practitioner accounts, with Christian and Muslim differences kept explicit.
art: Follow one object through making, use, collection and current stewardship; do not infer consent from a museum caption.
language: Build a dated example of speech-to-print transformation using inspected texts and a reviewed orthographic comparison.
women: Develop separate evidence dossiers for individual women and market offices; do not infer all women's experiences from elite biographies.
atlantic: Choose a named Atlantic community and documented local institution; show both transformation and limits of claimed continuity.
colonial: Use one inspected administrative file alongside local accounts; distinguish a colonial official's category from a community's own description.
heritage: Let conservation records, named Nigerian contributors and religious context shape the narrative; the grove pilot provides a parallel draft.
daily-life: Build a consented household or food-history case with place and period; avoid turning an illustrative example into a universal custom.
modern-world: Choose a dated cultural initiative with named creators and documented outcomes; separate contemporary self-description from impact evaluation.
know-alphabet: Add reviewed word-level examples for underdots and the digraph, with no claim that synthetic speech is an authentic speaker.
know-tones: Develop a linguist-reviewed minimal-pair sequence and explain limits of text-only pitch exercises.
know-oral-literature: Use one permission-cleared performance with narrator, occasion and translation history; do not fill missing lines from memory or generation.
know-dialects: Commission local speaker review of specific dialect examples; distinguish a spelling variant from evidence of a separate historical origin.
know-overview: Present locally scoped religious categories with clearly attributed differences; resist a single universal pantheon diagram.
know-ifa-faith: Develop public accounts of training and custodianship with named lineage scope; exclude restricted verses and predictions.
know-religious-change: Use inspected local mosque, church or print records to show one transition rather than extrapolating across Yorubaland.
know-orisa-guide: Explain category differences through three well-provenanced public objects or accounts; retain unresolved local terminology.
know-ogun: Pair a documented ironworking object with a separately attributed devotional account; do not turn association into technological priority.
know-osun: Specify river, shrine, town and source perspective; distinguish a water-related belief from ecological or clinical evidence.
know-shango: Separate royal memory, worship and diaspora developments; acquire evidence before assigning one biography to all traditions.
know-esu-orunmila: Trace a specific translation decision and a distinct public account of interpretation; do not collapse the two sacred referents.
know-indigenous-education: Develop a dated, place-specific learning example with evidence for teacher, learner and task; avoid an idealised universal precolonial classroom.
know-literacy: Read a primary printed item and document edition, orthography and institutional setting; a catalogue date alone cannot support its arguments.
know-learning-pathways: Follow a named apprenticeship account with permission and evidence for assessment of skill; separate stated mission from measured outcomes.
know-numbers: Add a linguistically reviewed counting example with explicit variant and arithmetic checks; do not claim it demonstrates a unique ancestral algorithm.
know-astronomy: Seek dated, local observations and vocabulary; distinguish a seasonal practice from a modern astronomical mechanism.
know-ifa-combination: Link to the preserved mathematical explorer and clarify positional encoding; require practitioner review for any authentic sign mapping.
know-environment: Develop a named land-use or conservation case with dated observations and local knowledge owners; avoid universal ecological wisdom claims.
know-medicine-overview: Require clinical and ethical review before expanding treatment claims; distinguish recorded practice from demonstrated safety or efficacy.
know-plants-language: Require botanical identification and consented vernacular context; never equate a shared plant name with a verified species or dose.
know-public-health: Source a specific care institution or practice and its period; clinical review must precede any health recommendation.
know-ase: Compare named philosophical interpretations without turning an English gloss into a universal or measurable substance.
know-ritual-knowledge: Develop a permission and restriction case study without disclosing the protected content itself; distinguish access from publication consent.
know-egungun: Invite locally scoped public accounts of roles and performance boundaries; no invented ritual sequence or identifying imagery.
know-marriage: Compare two documented local or generational accounts with participants' consent; avoid implying one ceremony is compulsory or timeless.
know-kinship: Use an anonymised, permission-cleared family record to demonstrate genealogy as evidence; protect living relatives and disputed affiliations.
know-birth-naming: Seek family-authorised naming accounts and reviewed language; do not diagnose identity, character or destiny from a name.
know-respect: Use consented everyday speech examples and local review; distinguish an ethical ideal from a rule every household follows.
know-festivals: Create a dated festival history from programme, organisers and local accounts; separate promotional description from documented practice.
know-food: Build one place-specific food biography with evidence for ingredient change and labour; nutritional or safety advice needs expert review.
know-clothing: Trace one documented garment's making and use; keep aso-ebi, aso-oke and resist-dyed cloth distinct rather than merging all dress categories.
know-governance: Develop a named town case with inspected office and council records; do not impose one constitutional template on all polities.
know-adire: Follow process, maker attribution and changing cloth records; the pilot separates documented objects from an invented teaching illustration.
know-metallurgy: Read excavation and technical analyses for one dated site; explain technical skill without claiming unsupported invention priority.
know-architecture: Use a documented compound or structure, dated plan and local account; avoid presenting a schematic as an authentic historic reconstruction.
know-performance: Commission a consented public performance account with occasion, musicians and language review; sound resemblance alone cannot prove speech encoding.
know-innovations-map: Give every proposed analogy its evidentiary boundary and a worked example; distinguish modern design inspiration from historical transmission.
know-digital-language: Audit one permission-cleared language dataset and evaluation task; preserve speaker consent, dialect and tone distinctions.
know-enterprise: Follow a named craft value chain with consent and documented transactions; verify wage or sustainability claims separately from marketing.
know-research-method: Work through one claim's source chain with explicit passage access; show how a correction changes an editorial conclusion.
know-atlantic-faith: Choose one community-specific religious history and its local sources; do not treat diaspora names as proof of unchanged practice.
know-future-archive: Turn the governance outline into a reviewed example of consent, versioning and withdrawal while keeping real private records out of the repository.
know-obatala: Separate public interpretations of whiteness and creation from archaeological chronology; consult named custodians on acceptable scope.
know-yemoja: Compare documented river and ocean associations in named communities; avoid allowing a global summary to erase regional practice.
know-olokun: Begin with a specific Owo material record and a separately attributed local account; distinguish symbolic wealth from physical causation.
know-osanyin: Keep plant knowledge, religious interpretation and clinical evidence separate; no formula or efficacy claim without specialist review and rights.
know-ibeji: Use one museum object's provenance alongside a consented family perspective; handle children, death and commemoration without stereotype.
know-gelede: Connect object details, named makers and author-mediated performance research; expand Benin/Togo voices only when passages and permissions are obtained.
know-regional-orisa: Develop Irawọ and Ilobu separately, with names, shrine-object provenance and public custodial review rather than a combined regional category.
sac-olodumare: Attribute theological positions and uncertain etymology separately; no universal doctrine or invented first speaker.
sac-esu: Prioritise inspected translation history and public Oyo-specific material; do not reproduce harmful Satan equivalence as a factual identity.
sac-orunmila: Separate corpus, specialist practice and mathematical teaching; a UNESCO record cannot certify a generated reading.
sac-obatala: Compare named regional public accounts and material associations; keep creation belief distinct from human-origins science.
sac-oduduwa: Treat palace genealogy and sacred narrative as attributed traditions; avoid a single independently verified ancestor claim.
sac-ogun: Choose a named community and documented working object; distinguish historical ironworking evidence from devotional explanation.
sac-sango: Anchor thunder, royal memory and staff imagery to separate sources; do not infer a unique historic person from an icon.
sac-osun: Link grove material records with clearly scoped public voices; do not let the Osogbo case stand for all Osun-associated communities.
sac-yemoja: Record the place, spelling and community for each water association; preserve differences from Atlantic devotional forms.
sac-oya: Follow a specific river or community account before expanding biography, colours or family relationships.
sac-olokun: Keep Owo-Yoruba, coastal and neighbouring Edo source contexts explicit; do not harmonise differing gender or origin accounts.
sac-osanyin: Document public shrine objects while withholding therapeutic recipes; botanical and clinical claims require separate expert assessment.
sac-sopona: Use dated public-health and historical records with indigenous perspectives; reject causation, cure or stigma claims unsupported by clinical evidence.
sac-orisa-oko: Trace a specific iron staff and its recorded shrine use; do not reduce agricultural traditions to a generic god-of-farming label.
sac-erinle: Prioritise Ilobu custodians and the cited shrine-object record; distinguish a local genealogy from a broad regional inference.
sac-oba-river: Obtain a named river/community version and rights before retelling; do not turn a moralised wife story into a universal biography.
sac-ibeji: Read an identified family or collection context; avoid stereotypes about twins and secure consent for any identifiable people.
sac-oshosi: Hold specific colour, kinship and ritual assertions until a documented local source is inspected; distinguish diaspora variants.
sac-osumare: Do not build a general theology from an archival finding aid; request the actual item and permitted contextual interpretation.
sac-ori: Separate named philosophical arguments about ori from other sacred categories and from the contested etymology of orisa.
sac-egungun: Seek locality, authority and recording boundaries for each public account; a costume photograph does not establish ritual meaning.
sac-gelede: Develop women's public perspectives and regional scope; avoid substituting a mask catalogue for a complete performance account.
sac-ajee: Commission a harm-aware review before expanding terminology; never identify living people as supernatural threats or treat accusations as evidence.
sac-categories: Build a reviewed glossary with named community scope; do not collapse ancestors, orisa and irunmole into interchangeable characters.
deep-myths-origins: Pair clearly attributed versions with commentary on genre; no reconstructed sacred dialogue or archaeological dating inferred from a myth.
deep-myths-storytelling: Develop a rights-cleared public example with transcript/translation provenance; explain whose interpretation is being presented.
deep-pronunciation: Commission licensed native-speaker recordings with dialect and linguistic review; preserve text-only honesty until they exist.
deep-faith-connections: Compare named participants' or inspected authors' perspectives rather than synthesising one combined theology.
deep-islam-history: Read mosque, manuscript and local-history records for a specified town and period; avoid unsupported first-arrival dates.
deep-christianity-history: Trace one church, school or printing record with African agency and source-of-source checks; no broad missionary narrative assumed independent.
deep-ghost-dna: Require genetics specialist review of model assumptions and uncertainty; do not convert an unsampled population into an identified ancestral people.
deep-cave-ashes: Use inspected archaeological dating and location evidence; distinguish the fossil's chronology from an asserted modern ethnic identity.
deep-ifa-tradition: Select public practitioner accounts with lineage, edition and permission metadata; keep restricted verses outside this pilot.
deep-ifa-odu-binary: Use the existing explorer as an explicitly modern positional model; authentic sign correspondence needs separately authorised practitioner review.
deep-geez: Commission comparative linguistic review of specific claims; superficial resemblance cannot establish descent or a shared lost script.
deep-political-system: Build a town-by-town civic case with named office holders and dated institutions; no universal oba/council constitution.
deep-names-morphology: Use linguist-reviewed examples with family context and permitted attribution; do not generate definitive personal-name histories from word splits.
deep-eleye-mothers: Prioritise custodial and safeguarding review; distinguish attributed belief, metaphor and harmful accusations without identifying alleged practitioners.
deep-obatala-deep: Trace each narrative episode to a named permitted version and inspected passage; avoid treating a broad overview as a universal liturgical account.
deep-modern-spiritual-world: Develop specific contemporary community cases and publication permissions; preserve religious difference rather than declaring one modern spirituality.
deep-name-olodumare: Obtain the original linguistic arguments and editions before expanding word-split history; keep author-specific proposals unresolved.
deep-name-orisa: Compare inspected linguistic arguments and dialect evidence; do not promote the ori-plus-sa analysis into a proven derivation.
author-sophie-oluwole: Read specific editions and page passages; quarantine Johnson-dependent history while treating the author's own philosophical argument with attribution.
author-ifayemi-elebuibon: Acquire authorised full texts and practitioner review before quoting verses or discussing protected knowledge; catalogue metadata is not a reading of the books.
author-wande-abimbola: Inspect identified editions and pages for literary method; keep bibliographic confirmation, verse access and reuse rights separate.
